einzeiler: The destruction of the Hood and the battle damage sustained by the Bismarck.
kurzfassung: The British battlecruiser Hood exploded and sank during the Battle of the Denmark Strait, leaving only three survivors from its crew of over 1,400. Meanwhile, the Prince of Wales landed crucial hits on the Bismarck, forcing the German leadership to reconsider their mission and head for port. The resulting damage and severe fuel leaks left the Bismarck vulnerable and easily tracked by British pursuers.
stichpunkte: The Prince of Wales scored a critical underwater hit on the Bismarck, causing a massive fuel leak.
A shell from the Bismarck struck the Hood's magazine, causing a catastrophic explosion that tore the ship in two.
Only three crew members survived out of 1,418 officers and men on board the Hood.
The Prince of Wales sustained repeated gun failures and underwater hits, prompting Captain Leach to lay a smoke screen and break off action.
British destroyers rescued the three survivors from the Hood while critically short on fuel.
Bismarck suffered flooding, a list, and a reduced maximum speed of 26 knots due to combat damage.
German commanders disagreed on tactics, with Lütjens choosing to abort the mission and head for St. Nazaire while Lindemann advocated for further engagement.
Leaking fuel left a clear oil slick that allowed British forces to continuously track the Bismarck.

clips.hook: An underwater hit creates a massive oil slick
clips.text: An incoming shell penetrates below the waterline and damages fuel tanks, leaving a distinct trail behind the vessel.

clips.hook: Witnessing the sudden loss of the world's largest warship
clips.text: Observers recount the shocking moment a massive column of fire engulfs the battlecruiser, leaving nothing behind in seconds.

clips.hook: Breaking off action to preserve the battleship
clips.text: The captain decides to deploy a smoke screen and retreat in order to regroup with upcoming reinforcements.

clips.hook: Thousands of tons of water flood the battleship
clips.text: Accumulated water intake introduces a noticeable tilt to the vessel that requires planned counter-flooding measures to correct.

clips.hook: A leaking fuel trail acts as a shining beacon
clips.text: The continuous loss of fuel forces the warship to drastically reduce its travel speed to reach a friendly port.

beschreibung:
The Battle of the Denmark Strait opened with British fire directed at the wrong German ship before Bismarck and Prinz Eugen concentrated their guns on Hood. This episode follows Hood’s catastrophic destruction, Prince of Wales’s withdrawal, the damage inflicted on Bismarck, and Admiral Lütjens’s decision to abandon the commerce-raiding mission and make for France while the Royal Navy remained in pursuit.
